# DATAMIMIC Community Edition

> MIT-licensed Python engine for deterministic synthetic data and pseudonymization.
> XML is the persisted executable project; DM JSON is its transient agent view.
> A project is a datamimic.xml entry plus acceptance/build.json, which holds its expectations and proof declarations.

Install CE 5.0 from PyPI: `python -m pip install datamimic-ce`.
For dataset tasks use the [consumer skill](plugins/datamimic/skills/generate-test-data/SKILL.md).
Its [setup skill](plugins/datamimic/skills/setup-datamimic/SKILL.md) installs CE in the project when needed.
Repository contributors read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and use `.venv/bin/datamimic`.

## Authoring

- [Codex / Claude Code plugin](docs/agent_plugin.md): installable steering for local CE and connected Platform projects.
- [Model review](plugins/datamimic/skills/generate-test-data/references/review.md): model structure, requirements, outputs and evidence for human inspection.

- [Agent guide](AGENTS.md): typed Build example, proof scope, DSL semantics.
- `datamimic authoring schema`: current DM JSON schema; `--name build_request_v5` for `acceptance/build.json`.
- `datamimic authoring capabilities`: compact CE vocabulary; `--full` includes contracts.
- `datamimic authoring capability --domain element --name generate`: one exact capability.
- `datamimic authoring reference --topic assembly --name model`: focused authoring guidance.
- `datamimic authoring build <project>`: prove the project; repair diagnostics; stop on `outcome=ready`, whose `artifact.files` bind every file it read.
- `datamimic authoring decompile model.xml`: transient DM JSON; expectations must be supplied again.
- Existing XML: `datamimic authoring lint model.xml`, then `datamimic authoring dry-run model.xml`; real execution uses `datamimic run model.xml`.
- [Worked Build projects](docs/examples/authoring.md): nested FK, memstore readback, time series.
- [Migration](docs/migrations/authoring-errors.md): frozen legacy intent compiler → XML and separate Build proof.
- [Destructive database operations](docs/guides/destructive-database-operations.md): clear, drop and selective delete, rules, logs, conformance cases.
